objective: Wire the external revenue loop so one revenue attempt can be followed from an external event, through Make and the ledger, into a GitHub route, and back out to PostHog and Stripe, under one correlation_id.
verified_revenue_note: No purchase has occurred. Every path below was exercised against real code and, where noted, real network calls; none of it produced or implies money. Revenue stays 0 until a Stripe payment record with payment_status paid exists.

verified_by_execution.claim: The github-only constraint is gone; four sources dispatch from one registry. A parallel session landed market/lib/source-adapter.mjs on main covering github/posthog/stripe while this work was in progress; rather than replacing it, `dispatch` was added to it and the parallel registry in the CLI was dropped.

result.github: LIVE. 41 signals fetched over the real GitHub API through the proxy; 30 expired on arrival and were persisted as EXPIRED; 11 decided.
result.posthog: AUTH failure, next_allowed_action HUMAN_REQUIRED - POSTHOG_PERSONAL_API_KEY and POSTHOG_PROJECT_ID are not present in this environment.
result.stripe: AUTH failure, next_allowed_action HUMAN_REQUIRED - STRIPE_SECRET_KEY is not present in this environment.
result.dispatch: LIVE. Ran end to end against a real client_payload file, before and after merging main.
result.unknown source: Refused, naming the four wired sources.

verified_by_execution.claim: The event bus cannot assert a payment.
verified_by_execution.how: A repository_dispatch payload containing (a) a PAYMENT signal claiming $69 and (b) a HUMAN_SIGNAL carrying forged PAYMENT_PROVIDER evidence was put through the real CLI.
verified_by_execution.result: Both refused: BUS_MAY_NOT_ASSERT_PAYMENT and BUS_MAY_NOT_SUPPLY_PAYMENT_EVIDENCE. Neither reached the store. The legitimate third event in the same payload was accepted.

verified_by_execution.claim: A redelivery is an upsert, not a second row.
verified_by_execution.how: The same dispatch payload replayed under a different dispatch id.
verified_by_execution.result: Pass 1: 1 new. Pass 2: 0 new, 1 already known. Ledger holds exactly 1 row with the same event_id.

verified_by_execution.claim: A signal the classifier calls ACTION can now actually become ACTIONABLE.
verified_by_execution.how: Same dispatch run, before and after the fix.
verified_by_execution.result: Before: status NEW, failure 'NEW -> ACTIONABLE is not an allowed transition', 0 actionable revenue routes. After: status ACTIONABLE via path [QUALIFIED, ACTIONABLE], 1 actionable revenue route.
verified_by_execution.note: This was a live defect on main. A qualified buyer with a live checkout was entering the store and being counted as zero.

verified_by_execution.claim: A dispatch can either carry the events or name a source to read.
verified_by_execution.result: client_payload.source named -> that feed is read (how Make turns a Stripe webhook into a real Stripe read rather than relaying a payment it may not assert). No source named -> the payload is the events, handled by the dispatch adapter under its refusal rules.
verified_by_execution.note: Both halves come from different sessions; keeping both is strictly better than either alone.

key_assertions: A PostHog checkout_click and the Stripe session it produced resolve to one correlation_id, derived independently on both sides from the client_reference_id the page writes.
An event that joins to nothing starts its own chain instead of sharing an empty-key bucket with every other unattributable event.
settlePayment - the shipped function, imported from the CLI - moves the correlated checkout to PAID then WON, stamps causation_id with the payment's event_id, and mints a deterministic action_id.
A payment does not settle a checkout on a different chain; the money is still recorded, and no route is promoted.
An unpaid session settles nothing and writes nothing, even on the correct chain.
Nothing is a winner without a payment provider saying money moved: a WON status with analytics evidence, a confident model, and an unpaid PAYMENT_PROVIDER record all yield zero winners.
Exploration stays open while there are no winners and closes with a recorded reason once one exists.
Winner resemblance breaks ties but never outranks a live payment.
Revenue is never summed across currencies, and a paid record with no amount is reported as unpriced rather than as zero.

not_verified: PostHog as a live source. Requires POSTHOG_PERSONAL_API_KEY and POSTHOG_PROJECT_ID in Actions; the adapter is exercised against fixtures only.
Stripe as a live source. Requires STRIPE_SECRET_KEY in Actions; the adapter is exercised against fixtures only.

The Supabase ledger against a real database. SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY are not present in this environment, and public.market_event_ledger has not been read or written. The adapter is verified against an injected fetch: it upserts on signal_id with Prefer resolution=merge-duplicates, projects the chain ids to columns, and returns the payload unchanged on read.
A real repository_dispatch from Make. The workflow leg is wired and its YAML parses; no Make scenario has called it.
Any purchase, of any kind, by anyone.

chain_vocabulary.source_event_id: the upstream system's own id, verbatim; never invented
chain_vocabulary.event_id: evt_<32hex>, deterministic from source + source_event_id, so a redelivery is one event
chain_vocabulary.correlation_id: cor_<32hex>, the revenue attempt; derived from the checkout reference that crosses the Stripe boundary
chain_vocabulary.causation_id: the event_id of the direct cause; null at an external boundary
chain_vocabulary.action_id: act_<32hex>, deterministic per correlation + asset + action

next_blocker: PostHog and Stripe credentials in GitHub Actions, and the Supabase ledger connection. Until Stripe is readable from a run, the standing question - 17 recorded checkout_clicks against 0 payment records - cannot be answered from either side.
